name: Strategy
intent: Define a family of interchangeable algorithms and let the caller swap them at runtime.
scenario: A checkout computes the price after a discount. Regular price, 20% off and $15 off are all different rules for the same job.
problem: Checkout has to apply different discount rules. Putting them all in one method with if/else makes the method grow with every promotion, and the rule is picked by a string instead of being an object you can swap and test.
solution: Pull each rule into its own object behind one small interface, apply(total). Checkout holds a reference to the current strategy and calls it. Swapping the rule is just assigning a different object.
pain: Checkout.total() has one branch per discount type
Every new promotion edits the same method
The rule is chosen by a string like "percent"
You cannot test one discount without running all the others' code
benefits: A new promotion is a new class or function, no edits to Checkout
The rule can be swapped while the program runs
Each rule can be tested on its own
whenToUse: You have several ways to do the same job and want to choose at runtime
A class has a big if/else or switch that selects between algorithms
You want to isolate rules so they can be tested and reused separately
whenNotToUse: There are only two stable options: a simple parameter or if may be clearer
The algorithms never change at runtime and share lots of state with the host class
Callers would need to understand every strategy to pick one well
pitfalls: Class count grows: in many languages a plain function or lambda is enough
Strategies that need lots of context from the host class leak its internals
Clients must know the strategies exist to choose one, so selection logic moves rather than disappears
Easy to confuse with State, which swaps behaviour automatically as an object changes

roles.label: Context
roles.description: Holds a strategy and delegates the work to it.
